newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-U.S. DENIES BALTIMORE ORIOLES' REQUEST FOR CUBA GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-U.S. DENIES BALTIMORE ORIOLES' REQUEST FOR CUBA GAME.

text.p: The Treasury Department on Thursday denied a request by the Baltimore Orioles baseball team to play exhibition games in Cuba this fall.
"The letter was signed and faxed to the Orioles' offices about one hour ago," a Treasury official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said on Thursday afternoon.
This was the second time the Treasury Department has refused permission for the Orioles to play in Cuba. They applied last year and also were turned down.

The Orioles organisation had no immediate comment on the decision, which came one day after Secretary of State Madeleine Albright threw out the ceremonial first ball at the Oriole's season opener against the Kansas City Royals.
A State Department official, who asked not to be named, said, "Under current policy licenses are not issued for professional sports in Cuba."
U.S. "trading with the enemy" law bars Americans from spending money in Cuba without permission from the Treasury Department.

Orioles owner Peter Angelos told the Washington Times while the request was pending that the requested trip was "for purposes of observing the Cuban baseball players who are among the best, if not the best, in the Central American areas."
